newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CELTRON JUMPS DESPITE PROFIT WARNING.
newsitem.headline: CELTRON JUMPS DESPITE PROFIT WARNING.

text.p: Shares in South Africa's Celtron Technologies Ltd jumped on Tuesday despite the firm announcing sharply cut profit forecasts for 1997 and 1998.
It said it expected to report a loss of 8.8 cents a share in the year to September 30 1997 and a profit of 16.26 cents a share in the year to September 30 1998.
In February, the company forecast earnings of 13.04 cents in 1997 and 70.18 cents in 1998.
However, dealers said the announcement had removed uncertainty about the stock. The shares rose 12 cents to 97 cents, but were still well down on their year high of 470 cents seen in February.
"The market hates uncertainty," one dealer said.
The company had previously cautioned it would not be able to achieve its prospectus forecasts when it reported a first half loss of 6.8 cents a share in May.

The company said on Tuesday the losses set out in the previous announcement reflected in the current accounts arose from the late launch of the Celtrack VMS System and the delayed launch of phones into the car rental market.
